A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentMark and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite added analyses, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original ALFWorld and ToolBench experiments, OASIS simulations, and watermark robustness and compatibility results in Section 5 and Appendices G–I.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds elicitation calibration, cross-run stability, Gemini evaluations, and capacity–entropy measurements in Appendix G.1.

M1.justification: Probability elicitation, differential recombination, CyclicShift encoding, and RLNC recovery remain unchanged. Using Context_t consistently in algorithms and appendices standardizes the shared-context formulation already present in v1; it does not establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: The evaluated coverage remains ALFWorld ID/OOD, ToolBench's six task subsets, and Twitter-like and Reddit-like OASIS environments. Added analyses reuse this coverage. Gemini is an additional model configuration, and adaptive attacks are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 adds a separately evaluated No-Induction greedy ReAct comparator alongside Baseline and AgentMark-F. Existing red–green, repetition-coding, no-watermark, and SynthID-Text comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: G.1.1–G.1.4 substantially extend evaluation design with a no-elicitation control, Gemini configurations, paired-run JSD measurements, and capacity–entropy analysis filtered to embedding-active steps. Existing main settings remain documented as before. G.1.1 calls Baseline elicited while G.1 retains a direct-ReAct description, so an actual baseline change or rerun is not established.

E4.justification: New analyses isolate the effect of elicitation, examine first-step versus overall distribution stability across runs, and compare capacity with entropy across tasks and models. These substantially expand scrutiny of utility preservation and capacity. Existing erasure, rewriting, and false-positive analyses remain; H.4 supplies discussion rather than an adaptive-attack experiment.

E5.justification: V2 Table 4 newly supplies standard deviations for retained aggregate AgentMark-F success rates, including ALFWorld-ID 89.3±30.9%; v1 Table 1 reported 89.3% with a baseline-relative difference. Three-run reporting and existing confidence-interval procedures are retained, without evidence of increased repetitions for the original experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 4–7 add calibration, stability, Gemini, and capacity–entropy results. For example, Gemini Base/Ours success rates are 70.6/67.8% on ALFWorld-ID, 71.7/72.8% on OOD, and 75.6/75.8% on ToolBench. Original benchmark and robustness values remain unchanged; these additions do not represent same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: G.1.4 adds an explicit mean-capacity versus mean-entropy upper-bound comparison and a mathematical argument for conditioning on embedding-active steps. The differential-recombination proof, CyclicShift capacity derivation, security argument, and RLNC rank bounds in Appendices A–E are retained without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: black-box behavioral watermarking, utility preservation, multi-bit capacity, partial-log recovery, and compatibility with content watermarking. Added evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly ties distribution preservation to elicited probabilities and adds interpretations involving structured deliberation and branching execution histories. New H.4 acknowledges that knowledgeable adaptive attackers can disrupt synchronization and that existing rewriting tests do not exhaust this threat space.

D1.justification: V2 documents models, sample budgets, and filtering rules for the added analyses, and clarifies the shared logged context required to reproduce seeds in Appendices C–E. Existing prompts, main experimental hyperparameters, and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to FDPSS and existing watermarking methods are unchanged. The reference-list change is an IEEE capitalization correction, not a citation addition or substantive repositioning.

P1.justification: Targeted edits align latent-versus-elicited distribution terminology and shared-context notation, add cross-references and acknowledgements, and organize new material into G.1.1–G.1.4 and H.4. The main narrative and overall appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 4–7 and extends Table 1's caption with an analysis pointer. The original false-positive table becomes Table 8. Existing figures and prompt boxes remain, with local relocation and page reflow rather than extensive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 supplements v1's utility evidence with Gemini evaluation and elicitation/stability diagnostics, while explicitly acknowledging adaptive-attack limitations. These provide useful additional validation. Gains are limited by inconsistent Baseline descriptions in G.1 and G.1.1, and Table 7's sub-one-bit capacity means despite its claim that every included step embeds at least one bit, which weakens the new capacity analysis.
